summary: Pre-registered online experiment (UMass Amherst, UW-Madison; NSF-funded) on whether programmers can judge LLM-generated postcondition assertions and whether LLM-written explanatory comments help. 86 retained participants (66.3% professional) each judged 10 stimuli drawn from 260 (26 HumanEval functions x 2 postconditions, correct or incorrect, x 5 comment conditions: none, exact, under-specified, over-specified, incorrect), using GPT-3.5/GPT-4 postconditions from Endres et al. 2024. Mixed-effects models on accuracy, confidence and time, plus a 10-person think-aloud study.

claims.claim: Programmers accept correct assertions far more reliably than they reject incorrect ones, with similar confidence in both.
claims.evidence: Correct 73.9% vs incorrect 49.0% accuracy (p<0.001, OR 2.94); confidence 3.98-4.14 with no significant difference (p>0.1). RQ1 is exploratory rather than pre-registered.

claims.claim: LLM-generated explanatory comments do not improve judgement accuracy.
claims.evidence: Pre-registered RQ2: comment presence has no significant effect (p>0.1). A null result, so small benefits cannot be excluded; no power analysis reported in text.

claims.claim: Low-quality explanations impair accuracy while increasing confidence.
claims.evidence: Only under-specified comments show effects, and against different reference groups: accuracy is lower vs exact comments (p=0.037, OR 0.58), while vs no comment the accuracy drop (54.3% vs 62.7%) is anecdotal; confidence is higher vs no comment (4.25 vs 3.99, p=0.005). Over-specified and incorrect comments show no such effect; no multiple-comparison correction.

claims.claim: Assertion completeness is only weakly related to judgement accuracy.
AI assistance may not improve the reliability of code comprehension and review.
claims.evidence: Generalised from postcondition judgement on HumanEval functions with older generators (GPT-3.5/GPT-4); no review task, no agent workflow.

patterns.note: LLM explanations as a comprehension aid were tested against no explanation and did not improve accuracy; under-specified explanations raised confidence. Prose explanations are not an effective comprehension safeguard here.
Human judgement as a gate on LLM-generated specifications is unreliable for incorrect items (49% accuracy, near chance), so approval alone is a weak safeguard.
Postconditions are formal acceptance criteria; think-aloud participants succeeded more when comparing clauses against the docstring one by one, but this is qualitative.
Relevant to specs generated by an LLM and then approved by humans; no spec-driven workflow is evaluated.

methodology.sample: 106 submissions -> 86 retained participants (66.3% professional, age 18-42), 10 stimuli each; 18 of 737 stimuli dropped for <20 s; think-aloud with 10 participants (50 pairs).
methodology.baselines: No-comment condition; correct vs incorrect postconditions.
methodology.models: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 postconditions (from Endres et al. 2024) and GPT-3.5-generated comments.
methodology.variance: Mixed-effects models with participant and stimulus random effects; p-values and odds ratios; no multiple-comparison correction.
methodology.ablations: Five comment conditions; demographics as covariates (no effect).

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint (10 pages, 6 figures); no venue stated.
standards.artifacts: Data, pre-registration and analysis scripts on OSF.
standards.preregistration: OSF pre-registration for RQ2; RQ1 exploratory.

biases.detail: Small HumanEval functions with single postconditions; real reviews involve larger code and domain context.
The abstract's 'impair accuracy while increasing confidence' combines effects against different reference groups for one of four comment types.
Generalises to AI assistance for code comprehension and review in general.
GPT-3.5/GPT-4-era postconditions and comments; newer models may write different explanations.

coi.affiliations: University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Wisconsin-Madison (academic).
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: OpenAI GPT-3.5/GPT-4 outputs; no vendor affiliation.
coi.detail: Some authors produced the prior postcondition dataset (Endres et al. 2024); findings cut against LLM-assisted specification workflows, so no favourable bias.

verdict_reason: Pre-registered, open-data human experiment with appropriate mixed-effects analysis and a robust main asymmetry. But the explanation-harm headline is a post-hoc composite of one comment condition against mixed reference groups, tasks are toy Python functions with older generators, and the broad AI-assistance generalisation is not supported.
applicability: Directly relevant to keeping domain-novice developers' comprehension: do not count agent-written prose explanations as a comprehension safeguard, since they did not improve accuracy and vague ones inflated confidence. For agent-written acceptance criteria in the spec phase, use executable counter-checks: run each criterion on known-good and known-bad ingestion examples (e.g. valid vs malformed healthcare-education content records), or use mutation testing. Keep criteria atomic and map each clause to a spec line, since clause-by-clause comparison helped in the think-aloud study. When evaluating onboarding aids, measure reviewer accuracy on seeded incorrect items, not self-reported confidence.
